$comment: Feature ledger for the portfolio site. Every user-facing capability is one entry. Statuses: planned → in-progress → done. A feature is 'done' only when every acceptance line is verified by at least one automated test tagged with its id (e.g. `@F-003` in tests/e2e/*.spec.ts or `[@F-003]` in a Vitest test name). tests/unit/feature-list.test.ts enforces this. Keep ids stable; append new features at the end.

features.title: Static export build
features.description: The site builds with `output: 'export'` into out/ and runs from any static host (GitHub Pages) with no Node server.
acceptance: `npm run build` produces out/index.html, out/robots.txt, out/sitemap.xml and the résumé PDF
out/ contains a .nojekyll marker so GitHub Pages serves the _next/ directory
No server-only APIs (headers, cookies, dynamic routes without generateStaticParams) are used

features.title: Sticky header with primary navigation
features.description: Fixed header with a monogram + name link, section links, theme toggle and a Résumé button. Gains a translucent blurred background once the page is scrolled.
acceptance: Header is visible at the top of every viewport and stays fixed while scrolling
Desktop navigation (`nav[aria-label="Primary"]`) is visible at ≥768px and hidden below
Every nav link points at an existing section id
Résumé button links to the PDF in public/

features.title: Mobile menu
features.description: Below 768px the nav collapses into a hamburger button that opens a full-width menu panel.
acceptance: Toggle button has an accessible name and `aria-expanded` that reflects state
Menu panel (`#mobile-menu`) is hidden until opened and lists every section link
Choosing a link closes the menu and navigates to the section
Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the toggle
Body scroll is locked while the menu is open

features.title: Dark / light theme toggle
features.description: Dark by default (matching the reference), with a toggle that persists the choice in localStorage and respects `prefers-color-scheme` on first visit. No flash of wrong theme on load.
acceptance: `html[data-theme]` is `dark` or `light`; first visit follows the OS preference
Clicking the toggle flips the theme and updates the button's accessible name
The choice survives a reload
All colors come from CSS custom properties so both themes are complete

features.title: Hero
features.description: Eyebrow (role · location), gradient display name, one-line pitch, availability badge, two CTAs (view work / get in touch), a stats row and a scroll cue.
acceptance: h1 is the person's name and fits inside the viewport at every breakpoint
CTAs link to #work and #contact
Stats row renders every figure from src/data/hero.ts and wraps to 2 columns on mobile

features.title: About section
features.description: Numbered section (01) with a one-sentence headline, the résumé summary, and a focus-areas card.
acceptance: Section has id `about` and the numbered eyebrow 'Profile'
Focus areas list renders every item from src/data/about.ts
Two-column layout on ≥1024px collapses to one column below

features.title: Experience timeline
features.description: Numbered section (02) with one card per role: title, company, dates, location, bullet achievements and tech chips; the current role carries a 'Current' badge.
acceptance: Every role in src/data/experience.ts is rendered in order with its bullets
The role flagged `current` shows a Current badge
Tech chips wrap without horizontal overflow on 320px

features.title: Selected work
features.description: Numbered section (03) with a card per project: kind label, status badge, title, description, outcomes and stack chips; external links open in a new tab.
acceptance: Every project in src/data/projects.ts renders as a card
External links use target=_blank and rel=noreferrer
Grid is 1 column on mobile and 2 columns on ≥768px

features.title: Skills & education
features.description: Numbered section (04) with grouped skill chips (from the résumé's Core Skills), education entries and languages.
acceptance: Every skill group and every chip in src/data/skills.ts renders
Education and languages render from src/data/education.ts
Groups flow 1 → 2 → 4 columns across mobile → tablet → desktop

features.title: Contact
features.description: Numbered section (05) with a call-to-action card: headline, email link, 'Send a message' mailto button and social icon links.
acceptance: Email link and button both use `mailto:` with the address from src/data/site.ts
Social links (GitHub, LinkedIn, Stack Overflow) have accessible names
Card stacks vertically on mobile

features.title: Footer
features.description: Copyright with the current year, a 'Built with Next.js · deployed on GitHub Pages' line and social icon links.
acceptance: Footer is a `<footer>` landmark containing the current year and the name
Social links have accessible names and rel=noreferrer

features.title: Scroll reveals and smooth scrolling
features.description: Sections fade-and-rise into view once; Lenis smooth scrolling on pointer devices. Both collapse to static when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
acceptance: Reveal wrappers (`[data-reveal]`) reach opacity 1 after scrolling into view
With reduced motion every reveal is fully visible immediately and Lenis is not started
Header active-state and theme transitions are also disabled under reduced motion

features.title: No horizontal overflow at any breakpoint
features.description: The page never scrolls horizontally and no element extends past the viewport edge from 320px to 1920px wide.
acceptance: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` ≤ viewport width at every viewport in feature_list.json
No visible element's bounding box exceeds the viewport's right edge
Side gutter is at least 16px on mobile
Interactive header controls are at least 40×40px on mobile

features.title: Accessibility baseline
features.description: Skip link, landmark structure, labelled controls, visible focus rings, and zero serious/critical axe violations in both themes.
acceptance: First Tab stop is a 'Skip to content' link targeting #main
Exactly one `<main>`; header, nav and footer landmarks present
axe-core reports no serious or critical violations at mobile and desktop widths in dark and light themes

features.title: Metadata, Open Graph, robots, sitemap and JSON-LD
features.description: Title/description from site data, Open Graph and Twitter cards, robots.txt, sitemap.xml and a schema.org Person record.
acceptance: `<title>` contains the name and role; meta description is non-empty
og:title, og:description and twitter:card are present
A `script[type="application/ld+json"]` parses to a schema.org Person with the name and sameAs links
/robots.txt and /sitemap.xml are served from the export

features.title: Active section highlighting (scrollspy)
features.description: The nav link for the section currently in view carries `aria-current="true"` and a visual indicator.
acceptance: Scrolling to a section marks its nav link with aria-current=true and no other link
Uses IntersectionObserver, not scroll handlers, so it stays cheap

features.title: Résumé download
features.description: The résumé PDF in public/ is reachable from the header button and the contact section.
acceptance: `a[data-testid="resume-link"]` exists in the header and the href returns HTTP 200 with a PDF content type
The link has a download-friendly label

features.title: Single-source content with no placeholders
features.description: All copy lives in src/data/*.ts. Shipped data contains no TODO/placeholder strings, and every nav link resolves to a declared section.
acceptance: No `TODO(`, `[Placeholder` or `lorem` strings anywhere in src/data
Email is a valid address; every external link is https
Every role has ≥1 bullet and ≥1 chip; every project has a stack; every skill group is non-empty
Nav links are exactly the declared sections, in order

features.title: CI and GitHub Pages deployment
features.description: Pull requests run lint, typecheck, unit tests, build and the Playwright suite; pushes to main deploy out/ to GitHub Pages.
acceptance: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on pull_request and push and uploads the Playwright report
.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml builds and deploys out/ with actions/deploy-pages
Both workflows use `npm ci` so exact pins are honoured

features.title: Consistent section chrome
features.description: Every section shares the same heading pattern: a dotted mono eyebrow, a two-digit index (01–05) and a display-font title.
acceptance: Sections about, experience, work, skills, contact render indices 01–05 in order
Each section's `<h2>` matches the title declared in src/data/site.ts
